assessment: This important study combines behavioral and imaging experiments to understand how levels of important brain chemicals shape the processing of information in the brain in children and young adults. The sample size and data quality are outstanding and some of the data are convincing. However, there are important caveats for some of the results, as discussed by the authors, and future replication will be important to fully substantiate the findings. This work will be of interest to neuroscientists, psychologists, and neuroimaging researchers investigating the developing brain in health and disease.
